description: Run a structured program/argv command. Every new command uses the selected approval mode. Plan commands may modify files when approved. Full access uses the host; Benchmark uses an offline task container. Runtime manages timeout and cleanup.

propertyDescriptions.executionScope: Default workspace sandbox. Request host for exact per-command host escalation; the approval includes full host filesystem and network access. Benchmark always remains container-confined.
propertyDescriptions.program: Executable name, path relative to cwd, or absolute local executable. Runtime checks links and executable identity; remote paths are not accepted.
propertyDescriptions.args: Literal structured argv, including multiline code and punctuation. Supply real arguments, not an extra launcher name. For cmd /c pass the whole command as ONE argument, e.g. ["/c","dir /b"]. Prefer search_files mode=list for directory listing.
propertyDescriptions.cwd: Absolute or workspace-relative directory. Workspace scope stays in the workspace; approved host scope and Full access may use other local directories. Benchmark resolves this directory inside its worker container.
propertyDescriptions.intent: Declared purpose, not permission or proof of read-only behavior. Use test, build or verify for validation.
propertyDescriptions.verificationKind: Optional validation category: unit_test, integration_test, build, typecheck, lint, format_check, smoke_test, benchmark, custom. Missing verify/test categories default to custom; build defaults to build. Invalid or inapplicable metadata is normalized without blocking execution.
propertyDescriptions.timeoutMs: An optional requested command-phase timeout. Runtime applies the minimum of this request, the configured command limit, and the classified capability limit, then returns all four timeout values including the effective limit.
propertyDescriptions.reason: A concise explanation of why this command is needed for the current task.

guidance: Prefer direct test runners and existing scripts; Runtime compacts display output, so avoid piping test output through grep just to save tokens. Multiline Python -c/Node -e, shell scripts, heredocs, pipes, redirects and synchronous nested calls are supported. Use start_command/poll_command for long work; bounded sleeps and timeout wrappers are allowed. Exit code and validation verdict are separate: an outer exit 0 does not prove tests passed. Unknown validation means insufficient evidence, not an instruction to rerun blindly. Command syntax is not a permission boundary. Background descendants are terminated when their command finishes; use start_command/poll_command to supervise long work. Never bypass network authorization, Benchmark isolation or sandbox failures; do not retry unknown execution or cleanup.
